scenario: Discussing weekend plans with a friend
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of French

vocabulary.note: used to connect actions in time
followed by a period of time
often used at the beginning of a sentence
can be at the beginning or end of the sentence
agrees in gender and number (prochain / prochaine)

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Qu'est-ce que tu veux faire ce week-end ?
dialogue.translation: What do you want to do this weekend?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Je dois finir un projet, mais ensuite je suis libre. On peut voir un film ?
dialogue.translation: I have to finish a project, but then I'm free. Can we see a movie?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bonne idée ! D'abord, on pourrait manger ensemble, et pendant le film, on choisit une chose à faire après.
dialogue.translation: Good idea! First, we could eat together, and during the movie, we choose something to do afterwards.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Peut-être, mais je ne veux pas trop tarder. Le prochain week-end sera plus libre.
dialogue.translation: Maybe, but I don't want to stay out too late. Next weekend will be freer.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Alors, on fait simple : on se voit samedi à midi, et ensuite on décide.
dialogue.translation: So, let's keep it simple: we meet Saturday at noon, and then we decide.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Parfait, je t'appelle demain pour confirmer. À samedi !
dialogue.translation: Perfect, I'll call you tomorrow to confirm. See you Saturday!

key_phrases.translation: What do you want to do?

key_phrases.phrase: On se voit samedi à midi.

scenario: Returning a faulty item at a shop
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of French

vocabulary.note: Used only in the third person singular (il faut).
In the context of a store, it means 'to return an item'.
Often used for 'to buy' (je prends ceci).

vocabulary.translation: to look for, to go get
vocabulary.note: Used to 'look for' an object or a person.
Indicates excess; often with an adjective or verb.
Also used as a reinforcement (je veux bien).
Conjunction that introduces an explanation, more formal than 'parce que'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bonjour, j'ai acheté cette lampe ici, mais elle ne fonctionne pas bien.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I bought this lamp here, but it doesn't work well.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Je vois, il faut retourner l'article, mais avez-vous le ticket ?
dialogue.translation: I see, you need to return the item, but do you have the receipt?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oui, voici le ticket. Je voudrais prendre la même lampe, s'il vous plaît.
dialogue.translation: Yes, here is the receipt. I would like to take the same lamp, please.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: D'accord, je vais chercher une autre en stock. Mais celle-ci est trop chère, peut-être ?
dialogue.translation: Okay, I'll go look for another one in stock. But this one is too expensive, maybe?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Non, le prix est correct, car c'est le même modèle.
dialogue.translation: No, the price is correct, because it's the same model.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Parfait, je vous apporte la nouvelle. Donc, vous pouvez l'échanger.
dialogue.translation: Perfect, I'll bring you the new one. Therefore, you can exchange it.

key_phrases.translation: you need to return the item
I'll go look for another one

scenario: Booking a table at a restaurant by phone
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of French

vocabulary.note: Agrees in gender and number with the noun.
Verb of the 3rd group; often used with 'de' for the recent past.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bonjour, je voudrais réserver une table pour ce soir, mais je sais que c'est tard.
dialogue.translation: Good morning, I would like to book a table for this evening, but I know it's late.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Pas de problème. Pour quelle heure ? Et pour combien de personnes ?
dialogue.translation: No problem. For what time? And for how many people?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: À 20h30, seulement pour deux personnes, parce que mon ami vient avec moi.
dialogue.translation: At 8:30 PM, only for two people, because my friend is coming with me.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: C'est bon. Avez-vous une préférence pour la table ? Près de la fenêtre ou au fond ?
dialogue.translation: That's fine. Do you have a preference for the table? Near the window or at the back?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: La dernière fois, nous avons adoré la table près de la fenêtre. Mais tout est bien si elle est libre.
dialogue.translation: Last time, we loved the table near the window. But everything is fine if it's available.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Parfait. Il nous reste une table près de la fenêtre, et elle est assez calme. À ce soir !
dialogue.translation: Perfect. We have a table left near the window, and it's quite quiet. See you this evening!

scenario: Describing symptoms at a pharmacy
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of French

vocabulary.note: Used in expressions like 'avoir mal à' (to have pain in).
Indicates a starting point in time that continues into the present.
In pronominal form 'se reposer' (to rest oneself).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bonjour, j'ai mal à la tête depuis hier.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I've had a headache since yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Avez-vous de la fièvre ?
dialogue.translation: Do you have a fever?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oui, un peu, et je suis très fatigué.
dialogue.translation: Yes, a little, and I'm very tired.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Avez-vous une ordonnance ?
dialogue.translation: Do you have a prescription?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Non, j'ai besoin d'un médicament pour la douleur.
dialogue.translation: No, I need some medication for the pain.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Je vous conseille de vous reposer et de boire beaucoup d'eau.
dialogue.translation: I advise you to rest and drink plenty of water.

scenario: Talking about your hometown to a visitor
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of French

vocabulary.note: Often used with 'ma ville' to indicate one's own city.
Agrees in gender and number: vieux/vieille/vieilles.
Attention: it can also mean 'place', but here it indicates the square.
Irregular: je connais, tu connais, il connaît. Used for people or places.
Used with verbs and nouns: beaucoup de monde, beaucoup aimer.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bienvenue dans ma ville ! Elle est grande, mais aussi très vieille.
dialogue.translation: Welcome to my city! It is big, but also very old.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Merci ! Je vois qu'il y a une belle place au centre. On peut marcher ici ?
dialogue.translation: Thank you! I see there is a beautiful square in the center. Can we walk here?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oui, c'est une place très animée. Il y a beaucoup de cafés et de petites boutiques autour.
dialogue.translation: Yes, it's a very lively square. There are many cafés and small shops around.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Parfait ! Et connais-tu une bonne rue pour acheter des souvenirs ?
dialogue.translation: Perfect! And do you know a good street to buy souvenirs?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oui, la rue Saint-Jean est parfaite. Mais attention, elle est très petite et souvent pleine de monde.
dialogue.translation: Yes, Saint-Jean street is perfect. But be careful, it is very small and often crowded.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Merci beaucoup ! J'ai hâte de découvrir tout ça.
dialogue.translation: Thank you very much! I can't wait to discover all that.

key_phrases.phrase: une bonne rue pour acheter des souvenirs
key_phrases.translation: a good street to buy souvenirs

scenario: Asking for advice on what to buy
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of French

vocabulary.note: Regular verb in -er, very used for shopping.
Masculine noun, often used with 'demander' or 'donner'.
Attention: it can mean both 'costly' and 'dear' (affection).
With 'bien' it means 'to like' (e.g., j'aime bien).

Verb in -er, attention to the root 'paie-' in conjugation.

dialogue.translation: I want to buy a gift for my brother, but I have no idea.

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.translation: Can you give him some advice? What is his maximum price?

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.translation: It's a good idea, but it's expensive. Do you have another cheaper option?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, je suis sûr que tu peux trouver un casque audio. Tu préfères payer combien ?
dialogue.translation: Yes, I'm sure you can find a headset. How much do you prefer to pay?

dialogue.speaker: A

scenario: Talking about past holidays
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of French

vocabulary.note: Used to indicate a duration of time.
Can mean weather or chronological time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Pendant mon voyage à la mer, j'ai visité des endroits magnifiques.
dialogue.translation: During my trip to the sea, I visited magnificent places.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Quel temps il faisait ? Tu t'es bien reposé sur la plage ?
dialogue.translation: What was the weather like? Did you rest well on the beach?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Le temps était vraiment parfait, et je me suis reposé sur la plage tous les jours.
dialogue.translation: The weather was really perfect, and I rested on the beach every day.

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.translation: Did you forget to take photos?

dialogue.text: Non, j'ai tout pris, mais j'ai presque oublié mon appareil à la plage !
dialogue.translation: No, I took everything, but I almost forgot my camera at the beach!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: C'était très bien ! Samedi soir, je suis sortie avec des amis.
dialogue.translation: It was great! Saturday evening I went out with friends.

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.translation: We ate together, then we saw a movie. And you?

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.translation: On Sunday I got up early to go running in the park.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Peut-être que je t'accompagnerai la prochaine fois, si je me réveille !
dialogue.translation: Maybe I'll join you next time, if I wake up!

dialogue.translation: Excuse me, to go to the museum, do I have to take the metro?

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.translation: Yes, take line 4, direction Porte d'Orléans. The station is right there, on the right.

scenario: Talking about your job to someone new

Conjunction of cause; introduces an explanation.

dialogue.translation: Yes, the team is important, especially after a long day. But every job has its challenges.

scenario: Discussing food preferences at dinner
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of French

vocabulary.note: Can mean 'dish' as a course or as an object.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Quel est ton plat préféré pour le dîner ?
dialogue.translation: What is your favorite dish for dinner?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: J'adore les plats sucrés, mais pour le dîner, je préfère quelque chose de salé.
dialogue.translation: I love sweet dishes, but for dinner I prefer something salty.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Moi, j'ai toujours faim avant de manger. Je peux goûter un peu de ton plat ?
dialogue.translation: I'm always hungry before eating. Can I taste a bit of your dish?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Bien sûr, mais ce n'est pas très sucré, c'est plutôt salé. Tu vas voir, c'est délicieux.
dialogue.translation: Of course, but it's not very sweet, it's rather salty. You'll see, it's delicious.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hmm, j'aime bien ce goût. Tu as un bon goût pour choisir les plats.
dialogue.translation: Hmm, I like this taste. You have good taste in choosing dishes.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Merci ! Maintenant, finissons notre dîner avant qu'il ne refroidisse.
dialogue.translation: Thanks! Now let's finish our dinner before it gets cold.

scenario: Asking for help with a computer issue
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of French

vocabulary.translation: to turn on, to switch on
to turn off, to switch off

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Mon ordinateur ne marche plus. L'écran reste noir.
dialogue.translation: My computer no longer works. The screen stays black.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: As-tu essayé d'allumer avec le bouton d'alimentation ?
dialogue.translation: Have you tried turning it on with the power button?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oui, j'ai appuyé sur le bouton, mais rien ne se passe.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I pressed the button, but nothing happens.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Peut-être que le courant ne fonctionne pas. Vérifie si la prise est branchée.
dialogue.translation: Maybe the power isn't working. Check if the plug is connected.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: La prise est branchée, mais l'ordinateur ne s'allume toujours pas.
dialogue.translation: The plug is connected, but the computer still doesn't turn on.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Alors, essaie d'éteindre complètement et de le rebrancher. Parfois ça aide.
dialogue.translation: Then, try turning it off completely and plugging it back in. Sometimes it helps.

key_phrases.phrase: vérifier si la prise est branchée
key_phrases.translation: to check if the plug is connected

scenario: Renting an apartment (first inquiry)
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of French

vocabulary.note: In the context of an apartment, 'pièce' refers to a room.
The monthly rent of an apartment.
Used for location, for example, close to the metro.
In real estate, 'visiter' means to see an apartment.
Here it means available (for rent or for a visit).
Administrative district in Paris; useful for location.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bonjour, je cherche un appartement de deux pièces proche du métro.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I'm looking for a two-room apartment close to the metro.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, j'ai un studio libre dans le 11e arrondissement, avec un loyer de 700 euros par mois.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I have a studio available in the 11th district, with rent of 700 euros per month.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: C'est un peu petit. Est-ce que je peux visiter l'appartement cette semaine?
dialogue.translation: It's a bit small. Can I visit the apartment this week?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, je suis disponible demain à 10 heures. Ensuite, je vous montre le quartier.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I'm available tomorrow at 10. Then I'll show you the neighborhood.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Parfait. Pouvez-vous me confirmer par email?
dialogue.translation: Perfect. Can you confirm by email?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Bien sûr, et je vous enverrai un plan qui permet de trouver facilement le bâtiment.
dialogue.translation: Of course, and I'll send you a map that makes it easy to find the building.
